full_text_en:
Lu Shunxu, Ning Nianci, Yu Defu — espionage case

Defendant: Lu Shunxu (ROLANOSLOO, also known as Lu Lan), male, 67 years old, citizen of the United States of America, residing at 6108 Damask Avenue, Los Angeles, California, United States of America. Arrested on December 23, 1985.

Defense Counsel: Yang Dunxian, attorney from Beijing Third Special Invited Law Firm; Yang Ying, attorney from Beijing First Law Firm.

Defendant: Ning Nianci, female, 42 years old, formerly an engineer at Beijing Construction Engineering Research Institute. Arrested on December 23, 1985.

Defense Counsel: Lei Qiong, attorney from Beijing First Law Firm.

Defendant: Yu Defu (husband of Ning Nianci), male, 48 years old, formerly a writer, director and cameraman at Beijing Science Education Film Studio. Arrested on December 23, 1985.

Defense Counsel: Han Lihong, attorney from Beijing First Law Firm.

The Branch of Beijing People's Procuratorate filed an indictment with the Beijing Intermediate People's Court, charging the defendants Lu Shunxu, Ning Nianci, and Yu Defu with the crime of espionage. After accepting the case, the Beijing Intermediate People's Court held closed trials on June 4 and July 9, 1986, in accordance with Article 111 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The following facts were found upon trial:

In June 1984, the defendant Lu Shunxu was invited to China by Beijing Institute of Aeronautics to give lectures. Before coming to China, Lu accepted a mission from the Kuomintang Military Intelligence Bureau of Taiwan, using the lectures as a cover to engage in espionage activities. After arriving in Beijing, Lu recruited the defendant Ning Nianci by means of material inducements and other methods to assist him in espionage activities. Subsequently, Lu directed Ning to directly contact Yang Peng (alias Yang Zongshan), a direct subordinate of the Kuomintang Military Intelligence Bureau stationed in the United States, who resided in San Francisco, USA. In March 1985, after Lu left China, Ning, under the direction of Yang and Lu, between April and September of that year, on three occasions provided Yang and Lu with several items of confidential intelligence and internal documents concerning China's economy and foreign affairs, under the pretext of sending items through outgoing Chinese personnel.

In mid-October 1985, Lu Shunxu, again on a mission from the Kuomintang Military Intelligence Bureau of Taiwan, came to Beijing and formally recruited Ning Nianci into the espionage organization. He taught Ning methods for secret writing and listening to instructions broadcast from the espionage radio station, and conveyed to Ning her alias, code name, and assigned tasks. During this period, Ning provided Lu with military intelligence. Lu and Yang successively provided Ning with espionage activity funds and remuneration totaling USD 810. In November of the same year, Lu went to Hangzhou, where he recruited Zhu Junyi (separately handled) into the espionage organization and collected from Zhu intelligence on military and economic matters. Lu also provided Zhu with a miniature tape recorder for espionage activities and RMB 260 in foreign exchange certificates.

Between 1980 and 1985, during visits to relatives in China, Lu traveled to Henan, Shaanxi, and other places, where through Xue XX, Chen XX, Lu XX, and Li XX, he spied and gathered intelligence on military and economic matters.

In November 1985, the defendant Yu Defu, knowing that his wife Ning Nianci was already involved in espionage activities, actively provided Ning with military intelligence and expressed his willingness to engage in espionage activities together with her.

The above facts are confirmed by physical evidence, documentary evidence, witness testimony, conclusions from forensic science and technology, and the confessions of co-defendants. The facts are clear, and the evidence is solid and sufficient to establish the charges.

The Beijing Intermediate People's Court held at trial: Although Lu Shunxu is a U.S. citizen, he joined the Kuomintang espionage organization and came to China twice on missions from the Kuomintang Military Intelligence Bureau to recruit members for the organization and engage in espionage activities, thereby serving the Kuomintang Military Intelligence Bureau of Taiwan. Ning Nianci, with full knowledge of the circumstances, joined the Kuomintang espionage organization, accepted assignments, and collected and provided military and economic intelligence to the Taiwan Kuomintang espionage agency. Yu Defu, although not a member of the espionage organization, also acted with full knowledge, accepted assignments, assisted Ning Nianci in espionage activities, and provided intelligence to the Taiwan Kuomintang espionage agency. The conduct of all three defendants constitutes the crime of espionage as provided in Article 97, paragraphs (1) and (3) of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. Lu Shunxu, Ning Nianci, and Yu Defu jointly committed criminal acts, constituting joint intentional crimes as defined in Article 22, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law. Lu Shunxu and Ning Nianci played primary roles in the joint crime; in accordance with Article 23, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, they are the principal offenders in this case and shall be given heavier punishments. Yu Defu played a secondary role in the joint crime; in accordance with Article 24 of the Criminal Law, he is an accessory in this case and shall be given a lighter punishment compared to the principal offenders. In accordance with Article 52 of the Criminal Law, counterrevolutionaries shall be additionally sentenced to deprivation of political rights.

On July 25, 1986, the Beijing Intermediate People's Court sentenced Lu Shunxu to twelve years' imprisonment; Ning Nianci to ten years' imprisonment with three years' deprivation of political rights; and Yu Defu to three years' imprisonment with one year's deprivation of political rights, each for the crime of espionage. In accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law, the property used by Lu Shunxu and Ning Nianci for criminal purposes was ordered to be confiscated. In accordance with Article 104 of the Criminal Law, a portion of the property of Lu Shunxu and Ning Nianci was ordered to be confiscated.

The defendants Lu Shunxu, Ning Nianci, and Yu Defu were dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance and appealed to the Beijing High People's Court, arguing that some of the criminal facts found in the original judgment did not match the actual circumstances, that the sentences were too heavy, and requested leniency.

The Beijing High People's Court, after a closed trial in accordance with the law, held that the facts of the crimes committed by Lu Shunxu, Ning Nianci, and Yu Defu as found in the original judgment were clear, the convictions were accurate, the sentences were appropriate, and the trial procedures were lawful. The grounds of appeal raised by the three appellants, including Lu Shunxu, were not sustainable. On August 20, 1986, in accordance with Article 136, paragraph (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law, the court ruled to dismiss the appeals and affirm the original judgment.
